newsitem.title: GERMANY: VW wants to build Skoda, A6 in India.
newsitem.headline: VW wants to build Skoda, A6 in India.

text.p: German car maker Volkswagen AG wants to build the budget Skoda model and the Audi A6 saloon in India, the government of the north German state of Lower Saxony said on Friday.

The Lower Saxony economics ministry said VW planned to build a complete car plant near Bombay costing several hundred million marks, over the next two or three years. Three factory locations have been short-listed.
The plant would have an Indian partner and would have capacity to make up to 60,000 Skodas and 5,000-6,000 A6s a year.
"The project is now being fine-tuned and should be finalised by the end of February," the statement quoted Lower Saxony economics minister Peter Fischer saying in New Delhi.
A spokesman for VW confirmed recent comments that his company was interested in entering the Indian market in a joint venture, but said that no final decisions had been taken yet.
"We are in a very concrete planning phase, but no decisions over investment, location or model have yet been taken," a company spokesman told Reuters.
Fischer was in India with a 16-member business delegation which included Skoda marketing director Detlef Wittig, and has met regional and national Indian government leaders.
Lower Saxony has a 20 percent stake in VW, which in turn has control of Czech-based Skoda Auto a.s.
